items.title: Mississauga to receive up to $401.4 million to support housing and community infrastructure
items.summary: The City’s efforts to make it easier to build new homes, including significant development charge reductions, helped secure the substantial new funding. 4 million in funding to help Mississauga build housing-enabling infrastructure including important new transit projects. Mayor Carolyn Parrish and Members of Council joined Ontario Premier Doug Ford for today’s official announcement alongside Rob Flack, Minister of Municipal Affairs and Housing, Jennifer McKelvie, Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister of Housing and Infrastructure and Member of Parliament for Ajax, and Peter Fonseca, Member of Parliament for Mississauga-East Cooksville. The funding, part of the Development Charges Reduction Program, helps municipalities who have reduced development charges invest in the infrastructure they need to support growth. It is part of the broader Canada-Ontario Partnership to Build. Mississauga was one of the first cities in Ontario to substantially reduce development charges – by up to 100 per cent – to help get more homes built and make them more affordable. The City has agreed to maintain these reductions until March 31, 2029. The new funding will help support housing-enabling infrastructure including two key transit projects: a new zero-emissions transit maintenance and storage facility and new downtown transit mobility hub. As Canada’s seventh largest city, significant investment in transit infrastructure is critical to support new housing development. These investments, which the City has long advocated for, will help support Mississauga’s growing population and deliver lasting benefits for residents and businesses. The City is planning a new zero-emission transit facility on City-owned land at 7300 West Credit Avenue to support future growth and improve service.

items.title: Severe storms impact Mississauga, but other Ontario regions were harder hit
items.summary: Powerful rain and wind storms that swept across the Greater Toronto Area and much of southern Ontario on Wednesday flooded some Mississauga roads and toppled trees in pockets of the city. com on Thursday. “A limited number of service requests were received related to localized roadway flooding and downed trees. ” City staff are also out on Thursday “assessing parks and trails to identify and address any additional storm-related impacts,” McCutcheon added. Peel Regional Police said dangerous conditions due to the heavy rain and strong winds were reported on Southdown Road and Bromsgrove Road in southwest Mississauga during the storms, which ripped across southern Ontario and the GTA Wednesday afternoon into the evening hours. A flooded Bromsgrove Road was closed for a period of time between Southdown Road and Winston Churchill Boulevard, but has since reopened, police said. Credit Valley Conservation issued local flood warnings and watches early Wednesday evening as multiple storms bringing heavy rainfall, unusually strong and damaging winds and in some cases hail moved across the region. Those warnings and watches were downgraded early Thursday morning as CVC said no additional rain is expected in the immediate future. Numerous communities in the GTA and southern Ontario saw main roads and highways flooded on Wednesday afternoon and evening, with many people in multiple regions also waking up Thursday morning to see significant damage caused by the strong winds.

items.title: Massive Mississauga development proposal revised in Ontario Land Tribunal settlement offer
items.summary: A massive Mississauga development proposal has been revised in an Ontario Land Tribunal settlement offer. The multi-phased development, proposed for 5100 Erin Mills Parkway, outside Erin Mills Town Centre, was for nine towers ranging from 20 to 44 storeys with a total of 3,162 residential units at Erin Mills Town Centre. The property is currently home to restaurants, a Bouclair Home, a medical and dental office, a pharmacy and a Dollarama. , went to the Ontario Land Tribunal due to council’s failure to make a decision on the official plan amendment and rezoning applications. The tribunal handles appeals when people, developers, or municipalities disagree on local planning issues, such as zoning bylaws and official plans. com this week. Under the new proposal, the building heights have been reduced from 20-44 storeys to 20-37 storeys. Building heights along Glen Erin Drive are 25 storeys, 20-storey buildings are at the northwest corner and 23-storey buildings are along Erin Centre Boulevard. The tallest buildings, at 35 and 37 storeys, are located toward the rear of the site. Two buildings exceed Mississauga’s 25-storey Official Plan maximum height permission, compared to five in the original submission, the spokesperson said. The 4,206 square metre public park has been relocated from the rear of the site to the northwest corner, providing a more prominent and accessible park with opportunities to establish synergies with the adjacent community centre and nearby schools.

items.title: Canada and Ontario Making Homes More Affordable in Mississauga
items.summary: 4 million for housing-enabling infrastructure in exchange for reducing and eliminating development charges over four years MISSISSAUGA, ON, Sept. 4 million through the Development Charge Reduction Program (DCRP) in recognition of its commitment to reduce development charges by 50 per cent for residential developments from January 29, 2025, to March 31, 2029. Furthermore, Mississauga is eliminating development charges altogether on rental units with one-bedroom plus den, two or three bedrooms until March 31, 2029. The funding recognizes Mississauga's early leadership in reducing development charges. It will help build more homes and community infrastructure while advancing the province's plan to protect Ontario by investing in projects that lower costs for families, support economic growth and keep workers on the job. The reduction in development charges over this four-year period is estimated to reduce the cost of building new homes by up to $36,140 per home. When combined with the up to $130,000 in savings enabled through the expanded HST relief on eligible new homes, these initiatives could save Mississauga families up to $166,140 off the cost of a new home. 8 billion over 10 years for infrastructure investments in Ontario, with Canada's share of the funding flowing through the Build Communities Strong Fund (BCSF). The two governments also agreed to provide relief on the full HST on eligible new homes from April 1, 2026, to March 31, 2027, saving homebuyers up to $130,000 off the cost of a new home. This is in addition to cost reductions for builders through the DCRP. Mississauga estimates that the construction cost savings over the development charge elimination and reduction period, along with the investment in housing-enabling infrastructure, would unlock 90,000 new homes, supporting a housing market with more choice and greater affordability for homebuyers and renters.

items.title: No flood threat, but people warned to avoid watercourses in Mississauga and Brampton
items.summary: A flood warning issued Wednesday night for Mississauga, Brampton, Caledon and elsewhere in the Credit River watershed has ended, but people are still urged to stay away from watercourses, conservation officials say. Credit Valley Conservation, the organization that protects natural areas and watercourses in Peel’s three municipalities and several other communities, said flood warnings and watches issued last night have been downgraded on Thursday morning “with no significant rainfall predicted” for the region. m. Thursday morning, noting “yesterday’s storm caused flooding and higher water levels. Streams and rivers remain dangerous. ” The statement and its urging that people stay away from all water bodies remains in effect through Friday, or until further notice. ,” CVC continued in its statement, adding more flooding is not expected. Conservation officials said “while no considerable rainfall is expected today, yesterday’s storm event brought isolated intense rainfall that caused flooding in localized areas and higher flows and water levels throughout the watershed. ” CVC added it will continue to closely monitor weather and water levels in the watershed. The local flood warnings and watches were issued as multiple storms bringing heavy rainfall, unusually strong and damaging winds and in some cases hail moved across the Greater Toronto Area and other parts of southern Ontario throughout the day and into the night on Wednesday.

items.title: Don Valley Parkway Reopens After Wednesday's Storm Floods Toronto and Mississauga Streets
items.summary: According to INsauga, heavy rain from Wednesday's severe storm shut down roads and highways across the Greater Toronto Area, including parts of Yonge Street and the Don Valley Parkway. The outlet reports the storm brought torrential rain, large hail and the risk of a tornado to wide swaths of southern Ontario, darkening skies over downtown Toronto and pummelling neighbourhoods farther north with hail. INsauga reports the flooding also suspended subway service during Wednesday's afternoon rush hour, and Toronto police said crews spent Thursday morning clearing debris from the Don Valley Parkway before its southbound lanes reopened. According to the outlet, Credit Valley Conservation issued a flood warning Wednesday evening after the upper watershed received about 70 millimetres of rain, with flooding also reported in Orangeville's First Street, Second Avenue and Rotary Park areas. INsauga reports Peel Regional Police said Bromsgrove Road in Mississauga also flooded, affecting vehicles on the road as well.

items.title: Keep road safety top of mind as the school year begins
items.summary: The City of Mississauga reminds all road users to slow down, stay safe and alert, as activity increases near schools and on neighbourhood streets. In the coming days, school zones, crossings and neighbourhood streets will become noticeably busier. The City is reminding drivers, transit users, cyclists, e-scooter users and pedestrians to be extra careful during the busy morning and afternoon school rush. With increased traffic and activity on the road, the risk of collisions is higher. Children can move suddenly and unexpectedly, so all road users are encouraged to stay focused, so everyone reaches their destination safely. When driving in a school zone, remember to: When walking, cycling, riding a scooter or taking a bus to school, remember to: To stay active throughout the year, some students prefer to walk, cycle or ride a scooter to school. Remember, it’s illegal and unsafe for kids under the age of 16 to ride an e-scooter. E-scooters may look easy and fun, but they are motorized vehicles that require a higher level of physical control, awareness and decision-making. For children under 16, non-electric scooters and bicycles are a safer choice. These activities help build balance, coordination and confidence while allowing younger riders to develop important road safety and cycling skills. Taking MiWay, the City’s transit network, is a great option for many students. Starting September 7, Route 110 University Express will run more often between City Centre Transit Terminal and Clarkson GO Station. As part of this change, Route 110A University Express will be discontinued, with service merging with Route 110 University Express.
